propositions.claim: The held text is the Federal Register printing of EO 13719 at 81 FR 7687.
propositions.quote: Executive Order 13719 of February 9, 2016 Establishment of the Federal Privacy Council

propositions.claim: Sec. 1 states a continuing policy (original scope, not proof of operation at the cutoff).
propositions.quote: it shall be the policy of the United States Government that agencies shall establish an interagency support structure

propositions.claim: Sec. 3 requires each agency head to designate a Senior Agency Official for Privacy.
propositions.quote: shall designate or re-designate a Senior Agency Official for Privacy with the experience and skills necessary to manage an agency-wide privacy program

propositions.claim: Sec. 4(a) establishes the Council as a standing forum.
propositions.quote: There is hereby established the Federal Privacy Council (Privacy Council) as the principal interagency forum to improve the Government privacy practices of agencies

propositions.claim: Sec. 4(c) gives the Council continuing functions.
propositions.quote: develop recommendations for the Office of Management and Budget on Federal Government privacy policies and requirements

propositions.claim: Sec. 4(d) requires continuing coordination with the CIO Council.
propositions.quote: The Chair and the Privacy Council shall coordinate with the Federal Chief Information Officers Council (CIO Council)

propositions.claim: The order contains no expiry or termination clause; sec. 5 is general provisions only.
propositions.quote: This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

verdicts.reason: Held official-printing text identifies EO 13719, February 9, 2016, at 81 FR 7687; heading quotation matches.
Section 1 contains the quoted policy and ongoing support objectives; this establishes original scope, not cutoff operation.
Section 2 expressly requires issuance within 120 days. It also separately requires agency implementation; the deadline does not terminate the order.
Section 3 contains the quoted designation requirement and additionally requires agency heads to work with the Council.
Section 4(a) contains the quoted establishment sentence and describes a continuing interagency forum.
Section 4(c)(i) contains the quoted recommendation function; the remaining subparagraphs impose additional continuing functions.
Section 4(d)(i) expressly requires the quoted coordination with the CIO Council.
Full held text contains no expiry or termination provision. Section 5 contains general provisions, including the quoted appropriations limitation and encouragement of independent-agency compliance.
